text: Version 2 of the regulatory requirements map is treated as the baseline immediately before version 3. Its issue date is written as the placeholder of Template and Rules R9 because no sheet states one, and version 3 is issued as Draft because no approval is recorded in any source of this run.
why: The run has no approval stop (R1 U8) and no source states the version 2 date or an approval; the change log still needs a row for version 3 and the document still needs a status.
read: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2 (sheets Obligations, By source, By process, Key; workbook properties) and Template and Rules R8.1 and R9.
applied_in: Sheet Read me, rows Document control (Date, Status, Approval, Change log)
impact: The change log shows the placeholder for the version 2 date and the status stays Draft; nothing else in the workbook depends on it.

text: The 32 obligations keep every cell of columns A to H word for word, and one owner service with its basis is added per obligation, taken from the controls in column F through the Ownership Map v1 and the Controls Catalog v4.
why: The realignment changes regulation to service only, and the workbook must keep every ID, number and date of the source while showing which service delivers each obligation.
read: Sheet Obligations columns A to H; Ownership Map v1 sheets Services, Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs; Architecture v5 slides 41 to 44; Controls Catalog v4 columns O and P.
applied_in: Sheet Obligations columns I and J; sheet By service
impact: The obligation text, the controls and the business owner are unchanged; the new owner service can be checked row by row through column J.

text: The owner service in column I is taken only from the controls the Controls cell names. Where a reporting or outbound-file leg of an obligation belongs to another service - P9 rwb-reporting for REG-15 and P2 rwb-integration for REG-27 - that service is named in the basis column and not in the owner service column, so column I stays a direct read of the controls.
why: No control in those two rows covers the reporting or outbound leg, and adding a service to column I without a control would invent an owner the source does not support.
read: Sheet Obligations rows REG-15 and REG-27; Controls Catalog v4 rows CTL-38 and CTL-02; Architecture v5 slides 41, 43 and 44; Ownership Map v1 table outbound_item.
applied_in: Sheet Obligations rows REG-15 and REG-27, column J; sheet By service note
impact: Two services that deliver part of an obligation are not counted as owners in sheet By service until a control names them.

text: REG-25 keeps S9 rwb-partner as its owner service because CTL-37 is the only control the row names, and the breach-notification step itself is recorded as having no owning object in the Ownership Map rather than being assigned to a service by guesswork.
why: The only defensible owner is the one a control fixes; the incident and breach process has no object, endpoint, event, workflow or job in the Ownership Map, so no service can be named for it.
read: Sheet Obligations row REG-25; Controls Catalog v4 row CTL-37; Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs; Architecture v5 slide 41.
applied_in: Sheet Obligations row REG-25, columns I and J
impact: The breach-notification process has no owner and no control until the Ownership Map is extended; the gap is P2.

text: Where the Controls Catalog v4 and this map disagree on which controls answer an obligation, the Controls cell of this map is kept word for word, the difference is stated in the basis column, and the owner service follows this map's Controls cell.
why: This document owns its Controls cells; a version that silently imported another document's list would change numbers the run must keep.
read: Sheet Obligations column Controls rows REG-11, REG-22, REG-27 and REG-32; Controls Catalog v4 sheet Controls column L rows CTL-43 and CTL-44.
applied_in: Sheet Obligations rows REG-11, REG-22, REG-27 and REG-32, column J
impact: P1 rwb-source-data is named for REG-11 and REG-27 by both documents; for REG-22 and REG-32 it appears only in the basis note.

text: REG-02 and REG-08 keep P9 rwb-reporting as owner service, carried from CTL-39 and from the ruling recorded in the Controls Catalog v4 (ASM-B-CTRL-32-4), and the dependency on that ruling is named in the row.
why: The two obligations are met only by the conduct sample; its owner is the best evidence available, and the assumption behind it is stated rather than hidden.
read: Sheet Obligations rows REG-02 and REG-08; Controls Catalog v4 row CTL-39 and its issue CG-B-CTRL-32-4.
applied_in: Sheet Obligations rows REG-02 and REG-08, columns I and J
impact: If the conduct sample moves to another service, the owner service of two obligations changes with it.

text: No wave or release column is added to the obligations. The wave of each service is written in the basis column and in sheet By service, and no epic or date is invented for an obligation.
why: An obligation states no release and the sources give a first release only for the controls; a wave column would have to be derived and could be read as a commitment.
read: Sheet Obligations, whole sheet; Controls Catalog v4 column First in; Template and Rules R5.6 and R1 U7.
applied_in: Sheet Obligations column J; sheet By service column D
impact: Per-wave coverage of an obligation is read from the basis text and the By service sheet, not from a column.

text: Column G Owner, the business role, and column I Owner service, the service that holds the control evidence, are both kept, and the Read me states that they are different dimensions.
why: Dropping the business owner would lose an ID and a value of the source; dropping the service owner would leave the realignment undone, so both are kept and explained.
read: Sheet Obligations column Owner; the version 2 sheet has no service column; Architecture v5 slide 41.
applied_in: Sheet Read me, row Owner column and owner service
impact: No row changes; a reader sees two owners per obligation and is told what each means.
